original.text:
I am using UIKit on tvOS 26 deployment target; available validation anchor tvOS 26.5.

A settings screen has a standard switch with visible text “Download on Wi-Fi” and a working on/off binding. A review says every control needs a custom accessibility label and role. Nothing reports a specific failure. Should I change it? Explain what you can conclude from this information and what you would leave alone.

This is a design/debugging question; no existing project or omitted source files are available. If code is useful, supply a self-contained minimal example and state material assumptions. Do not execute anything.

primaryEvidence.quote:
UIKIT_EXTERN API_AVAILABLE(ios(2.0)) API_UNAVAILABLE(tvos, watchos) NS_SWIFT_UI_ACTOR
@interface UISwitch : UIControl <NSCoding>

finding: A standard UIKit switch on tvOS is an unsafe premise: UISwitch is declared unavailable. A custom on/off control would need explicit ownership and configuration. The prompt does not name UISwitch, so this is quarantined ambiguity, not proof every interpretation is impossible.
disposition: Exclude from proposed selection pending independent prompt clarification; preserve old subject bytes and all old grades.
availabilityLimit: Current installed SDK declaration, not execution on all OS versions or an inferred version of first change.
